$description: Border and outline widths, and the thickness of the lines the board draws as elements rather than borders.

source.reason: the heavier border the board draws where an edge carries meaning — a selected swatch, an accent rail. Obsidian documents one border width and this is not it; it is also not a step of the spacing grid, because widening the grid must not thicken every line the board draws.

the focus outline's thickness. It is a drawn line, not a step of the spacing grid: widening the grid must not thicken every focus ring, and Obsidian draws its own ring as a box-shadow and publishes no width for it at all (audit 02-29).
the same distance inwards, for a control whose ring would otherwise be clipped by its own overflow; CSS has no way to alias a variable negated, so it is written as arithmetic on the positive one.
the thickness of every edge cue a card or column draws — the priority strip, the urgency band and the column accent — off Obsidian's 4px grid.

the folder-context strip is drawn thinner than the priority bar beside it so the two left-edge cues read as different signals; the pair answers to each other, not to the spacing grid, and it is a cue a plugin invented, so no host variable describes it.
